title: Your Bank Just Got Stricter: New Rules Against Mis-Selling Financial Products
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced new rules against banks mis-selling financial products. These rules became effective from July 1, 2026.

faq.q: What kind of financial products does this cover?
faq.a: This framework covers various financial products sold by banks, including insurance policies, mutual funds, investment products, and loans.

faq.q: What should I do if I suspect I've been mis-sold a product?
faq.a: First, gather all relevant documents and communications. Then, formally complain to your bank. If the bank doesn't resolve it to your satisfaction, you can escalate the matter to the RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme.

faq.q: Does this apply to all banks in India?
faq.a: Yes, the framework applies to commercial banks. While some sources mention it generally covers "all bank customers", some draft directions specifically exclude small finance banks, payments banks, regional rural banks, and local area banks. For most common banking relationships, it applies.

faq.q: Will I get all my money back if mis-selling is proven?
faq.a: The rules state you could be eligible for a full refund or compensation for the financial loss suffered due to mis-selling. The exact amount would depend on the specifics of your case and the loss incurred.
